ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side of the upper branch is inductor L, and the right side is resistor R, the two being connected in series. The voltage corresponding to inductor L is labeled 80 V, and the voltage corresponding to resistor R is labeled 60 V. The voltmeter V in the lower branch is connected across the entire series L-R branch, so it measures the total AC voltage across the series combination of L and R. Reasoning: In a series R-L AC circuit, the voltage V_R on the resistor is in phase with the current, and the voltage V_L on the inductor leads the current by 90°, so V_R and V_L are mutually perpendicular phasors. The RMS value of the total voltage is the magnitude of the phasor sum: V = sqrt(V_L^2 + V_R^2) = sqrt(80^2 + 60^2) = sqrt(6400 + 3600) = sqrt(10000) = 100 V. Therefore the voltmeter reading is 100 V.
